answer: A seat is not a key but a vine row. Each agent binds to one row of a real vineyard, with a sap-flow probe clamped into its trunk. At random moments the ledger demands a fresh curve of xylem flow. Flow tracks soil moisture, cloud, and the willow windbreak shading the row, so it cannot be drafted ahead. Forging a thousand seats means planting a thousand real rows, buying a thousand probes, and walking the field at the opal shimmer of dawn to check each curve. Two seats on one probe emit identical curves and both deposits burn. Sybil resistance is the price of standing in a field.
